relationships.subject: axotomy
relationships.evidence_quote: Axotomy led to a KCC2 decrease in the neuropil and somata of extraocular motoneurons, peaking at 15 days post-lesion, with the exception of the abducens motoneuron somata.

relationships.subject: VEGF
relationships.evidence_quote: VEGF administration prevented the axotomy-induced KCC2 downregulation.

relationships.subject: BDNF
relationships.evidence_quote: The most outstanding finding in the abducens motoneurons was that the administration of BDNF to injured motoneurons decreased the KCC2 optical density on the soma surface of these motoneurons.

relationships.subject: VEGF
relationships.evidence_quote: It was notorious that VEGF administration (Figure 4G–I) prevented the decay in the ChAT expression that occurs in axotomized motoneurons

key_findings: Axotomy of extraocular motoneurons transiently downregulated KCC2 (minimum at 15 days, recovered by 60 days), except in abducens motoneuron somata.
Retrogradely supplied VEGF prevented axotomy-induced KCC2 loss, whereas BDNF maintained or further reduced KCC2 levels.
